question: do U-Net skips and attention gates improve learning per training token on TinyMoE R1 (recipe-stack)?
workload: TinyMoE finer experts 32 x 384 top-4, 12 physical layers with layers 3-8 visited twice, B2 x 1024, 655,360,000 tokens, Latch programs only; seeds 1911-1913

verdicts.D: both help on 3/3 seeds: 0.97-0.99x tokens to 3.30, test -0.008 mean; about 1.05x measured update seconds to 3.30

unresolved: D (pack-g3-sg) fails one FP64 trained-state audit update: layer-6 input_layernorm gain gradient rel-L2 0.101 vs gate 0.08 (the other update passes at 0.048); reported as a limitation, not waived

rpackb (norm_fusion fused backward RoPE/GQA unpack) produces wrong k_proj gradients when a per-head gate sits between attention and o_proj (rel-L2 up to 0.51); not root-caused; C/D were rebuilt without rpackb; the lane compiled with source byte-identical to the released 0.9.0rc1 compiler (no src/ difference), so the defect is present in the release; packaged workloads do not have this graph and pass their audits
whether the D gain comes from input-dependent gating or from halving attention is not established
